cards.title: SAINT feels alive
cards.body: Say "Hey SAINT" and she pops up from the taskbar and listens. She sits on your windows, dances when Spotify plays, walks around on her own and watches your cursor.
cards.details: Drop her on a window and she sits on its top edge and moves with it. She picks the spot that hides the least of what you're doing, stays on one of your monitors, and learns where you like her. Animations you ask for now play to the end instead of snapping back to standing. She never takes your keyboard: typing in the Store or a game keeps going to it.
cards.how:
Say "Hey SAINT", or drag her onto a window.
Right-click her for Head and shoulders / Full body, size and animations.
While she's on screen you can talk to her for about 20 seconds without the wake word (not during games or calls).

cards.title: Your monitor's speakers, and a real mixer
cards.body: HDMI and DisplayPort sound from NVIDIA cards no longer disappears, Bluetooth stays in high quality, and Settings › Sound is a mixer: every output, each app's output and volume, several outputs at once.
cards.details: HalOS keeps the NVIDIA HDMI/DP audio device on and awake, so a monitor with speakers shows up by name. Bluetooth headphones no longer drop into the choppy headset mode just because the microphone is on. Fix the sound now really repairs it: it turns a switched-off card back on, picks a plugged-in output, moves playing apps and says what it did.
cards.how:
Settings › Sound: pick an output (Turn on and use), press Test to hear it.
Under Apps, choose where each app plays.
Tick two outputs and choose Play on the checked outputs.
No sound? Press Fix the sound, or say "fix my sound".

cards.title: A smarter SAINT that doesn't interrupt
cards.body: SAINT chats like a person, knows your PC and what HalOS can do, starts fresh each time you open it, and never pulls you out of what you're doing.
cards.details: When Claude Code is signed in, chat uses a small fast Claude model; offline it uses your local model with better knowledge of the system. Passing problems ("my sound isn't working") are no longer remembered forever. Background work stays on its own desktop: you can watch SAINT work on one desktop and play a game on another.
cards.how:
Talk to SAINT as usual.
Settings › AI: choose the local model; chat through Claude turns on by itself when Claude Code is signed in.

cards.title: The Halo is its own app
cards.body: The glow around the screen runs as its own app, so the SAINT icon on the taskbar always opens SAINT.

cards.title: Evolve with Claude Code, and SAINT Vault
cards.body: Evolve works again with a signed-in Claude Code, and shows a Sign in button when it isn't. Obsidian comes with HalOS, and SAINT Vault in Documents is SAINT's notes and memory.
cards.details: Every Claude Code run SAINT starts can read SAINT Vault: notes on what HalOS can do, this PC, and the facts SAINT remembers about you. The Obsidian skills (Markdown, Bases, Canvas) are installed for Claude on first run.
cards.how:
SAINT › Evolve: describe what to change, or press Sign in to Claude Code first.
Open Obsidian and pick Documents › SAINT Vault to read and edit SAINT's notes.

cards.title: Migrate from Windows, your way
cards.body: Browse your whole Windows drive and tick what to bring, add your own Quick add shortcuts, pick which Windows to read, and Wallpaper Engine wallpapers come along. One failed file no longer stops the rest.
cards.how:
Settings › Migrate from Windows.
Right-click a folder › Add to Quick add… for your own shortcut.
Failed items are listed at the end with Retry.

cards.title: Files: Downloads, Trash and real screenshots
cards.body: HalOS Files shows every download and install in its sidebar (with Cancel for Store installs) and your Trash. Print now lets you drag an area to screenshot.
cards.how:
Print: drag an area. Shift+Print: all screens. Meta+Print: the active window.
Say "screenshot of an area" to SAINT.

cards.title: A Task Manager you can read
cards.body: Every Task Manager tab now looks like Processes: plain words, search, clear numbers that sort correctly, and summaries.

cards.title: HalOS Wallpapers
cards.body: A new app for every wallpaper you have: SAINT's living wallpaper, your Wallpaper Engine wallpapers and your pictures.
cards.details: It finds every Wallpaper Engine wallpaper Steam downloaded, on HalOS and on your Windows drive, and shows them with their previews and whether each is a scene, a video or a web wallpaper.
cards.how:
Open HalOS Wallpapers from the app menu, or say "open wallpapers".
Pick a wallpaper, choose a monitor (or all), then Apply.
On a dual-boot PC, choose Look on Windows drives to add the ones from Windows.
Scene and web wallpapers need Wallpaper Engine support: the app installs it with one click.

cards.title: Window animations you choose
cards.body: Pick how windows open, close, minimize and switch desktops, each at its own speed. Nothing changes until you press Save.
cards.details: Profiles bundle all four: SAINT, Supernova, Snappy, Calm and Off come built in, and you can make, rename and delete your own. The SAINT star now plays all the way through and shrinks evenly.
cards.how:
Settings > Animations. Choose a profile, or a window event and what it plays.
The preview shows every change; Try on a real window plays it once on a test window.
Save puts it on your windows; Revert goes back.

cards.title: SAINT Visualizer widget
cards.body: The SAINT logo and its visualizer on a clear background, over any wallpaper: a picture, a slideshow or Wallpaper Engine.
cards.details: It moves with SAINT's voice, the music playing, your microphone or a slow breath, as bars under the logo or a ring around it. Sound levels are read live on this PC; nothing is recorded.
cards.how:
Choose Try it (or Settings > Wallpaper > Add the visualizer as a widget).
Drag the widget and its edges to place and size it.
Right-click it > Configure for what it moves with, its style and colour.

cards.title: A wallpaper that listens
cards.body: The living wallpaper: a colour or gradient with the SAINT logo anywhere, glowing and moving with SAINT's voice, your music or the microphone.
cards.how:
Settings > Wallpaper: colours, logo size and place, bars or a ring, what it moves with, per monitor.
Use the glow colour as the accent everywhere, or make a slideshow from a folder of pictures.

cards.title: Start from another device
cards.body: The boot menu and Recovery list every disk and USB stick, and Windows, so you can start from any of them.

cards.title: SAINT updates in place
cards.body: SAINT updates itself without reinstalling HalOS, and if an update misbehaves, roll back to the previous one.

cards.title: Passwords
cards.body: Your logins in the system keyring: copy, fill in, one-time codes, and import from Apple Passwords, Chrome, Firefox or Bitwarden.
